title: Spatio-Temporal In Vivo Imaging of Ocular Drug Delivery Systems using Fiberoptic Confocal Laser Microendoscopy
protocol: Dissolve 1 g of Evans Blue in 50 mL of sterile saline to make a 2% EB dye solution.
Filter the EB solution using 0.22 μm filters into 1.5 mL sterile tubes.
Store filtered EB solution at room temperature for later use.
Add POPC/Fl-DHPE (95:5) in chloroform/methanol (2:1) to a 100 mL round bottom flask.
Use a rotary evaporator at 150 rpm and 40°C with vacuum maintained at 0 mbar for 1 hour to create a thin lipid film.
Hydrate the lipid film with phosphate-buffered saline at 40 °C to form multi-lamellar vesicles (MLV).
Load the MLVs into a glass syringe for manual extrusion through a 0.08 µm pore size polycarbonate filter, repeating 30 times.
Filter the liposomes through a 0.22 µm sterile syringe filter.
Confirm the hydrodynamic diameter of the liposomes using a dynamic light scattering system.
Inject mouse with EB IV via the tail vein (2.5 mg/kg), 2 hours before subconjunctival injection.
Sedate the mouse using 5% isoflurane in an induction chamber until adequate anesthesia is achieved.
Maintain sedation at 2%-2.5% isoflurane while on a heating pad throughout the procedure.
Trim whiskers near the eye to be injected.
Instill a drop of topical anesthetic 0.5% proxymetacaine hydrochloride solution directly on the eye.
Load a 10 µL glass syringe with fluorescent liposomes (Fl-DHPE: 0.78 mg/kg) and dispel all air bubbles in the syringe prior to injection.
Inject the subconjunctival space of the mouse with the prepared liposome solution.
Using a tweezer, lift the conjunctiva slightly and inject slowly into the subconjunctival space.
Withdraw the needle slowly to prevent backflow.
Ensure that a visible bleb filled with fluorescent liposomes is formed.
Administer a drop of antibiotic 1% fusidic acid on the eye after the injection.
Monitor the mouse until it regains consciousness.
Switch on the CLM system.
Clean the connector of the scanning probe using an optical connector cleaner according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Position the connector in contact with the cleaning ribbon and slide the connector along the ribbon while maintaining contact.
Clean the distal tip (also known as the scanning tip) of the probe by dipping it into the cleansing solution, followed by the rinsing solution provided by the manufacturer.
Connect the probe to the CLM system.
Choose the Field of view (FOV).
Locate the acquisition files for the setup.
Allow the system to warm up for 15 min as instructed.
Calibrate the system according to the manufacturer's instructions using the calibration kit.
Immerse the tip in the cleansing vial followed by the rinsing vial (5 s in each vial).
Leave it in the air for background recording for both channels.
Immerse the tip in the fluorophore 488 nm vial for 5 seconds to normalize signal values from different fibers in the probe.
Immerse the tip in the cleansing vial followed by the rinsing vial (5 s in each vial).
Immerse the tip in the rinsing vial until the fluorescence signal recorded disappears.
Immerse the tip in the fluorophore 660 nm vial to normalize signal values from different fibers in the probe.
Calibrate the probe.
Check background values for the probes.
Clean the probe with a cotton tip applicator if background values are above 100/defined user value or if the probe appears dirty.
Repeat cleaning and calibration until background values are below the defined maximum.
Define the maximum background value to ensure consistent probe conditions.
Switch on the animal temperature controller (ATC).
Adjust the ATC to 37 °C.
Cover the heating pad with a surgical drape.
Fix the nose cone on the heating pad.
Clamp the stand of the dissecting microscope to the tabletop.
Rotate and adjust the eyepiece of the microscope ergonomically for viewing the mouse eye.
Sedate the mouse using 5% isoflurane in an induction chamber.
Transfer the mouse to the nose cone once non-responsive.
Maintain sedation at 2%-2.5% isoflurane while on a heating pad throughout the procedure.
Trim the whiskers of the mouse.
Instill a drop of 0.5% proxymetacaine hydrochloride solution onto the mouse's eye.
Drop several drops of saline onto the ocular surface to clean the eyes.
Adjust the microscope for direct focus at 0.67x magnification on the mouse eye.
Lubricate the eyes with saline throughout the imaging session.
Turn on the laser and place the probe directly onto the region to be imaged on the eye.
Start recording acquisition to observe fluorescence in the eye's specified regions.
Hold the probe like a pen during imaging.
Stop the recording when all flagged and labeled regions have been imaged.
Export image acquisition files using the CLM acquisition software.
Choose File | Export and select the desired format for export.
Adjust look up table (LUT) settings as needed for accurate fluorescence intensity comparison.
Use the same LUT thresholds adjusted to those of the control mouse with no liposomes injected.
Open exported images in an appropriate image processing software like ImageJ.
Draw the region of interest (ROI) for analysis.
Keep ROI consistent across all images by using the same area.
Measure and record green fluorescence values within the ROI.
Enter measured values into a spreadsheet.
Calculate and tabulate average and fluorescence intensity (a.u.) values for the ROI.
Euthanize the mouse according to local IACUC-approved methods.
Enucleate the eye after euthanasia.
Fix the enucleated eye in 1 mL of 4% formaldehyde or 10% formalin solution overnight.
Trim excess fats from the eye.
Embed the eye in Optimal Cutting Temperature (OCT) compound.
Keep the embedded eye frozen at -80°C for at least one day.
Cut sections of 5 μm thickness in a cryostat with cutting temperature maintained at 20°C.
Transfer the section to a Poly-L-Lysine-coated microscope slide.
